name: Join-Many Skips Reordering Order-Preserving Left Batches

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Join-Many Skips Reordering Order-Preserving Left Batches Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`JoinManyState::apply_left` builds the desired order twice per batch (ranks before the updates, the reorder target after); each build tests every group for emptiness under its lock, so one left update into a 10k-row `left_join_many` costs 550 µs. A left batch that only updates or refreshes keys in place keeps the left order, creates no group and removes no key; if the result also gains or loses no key, its order is already the desired one. Building the ranks only when a result key is added and reordering only when the left order or the result's key set changed gives identical output in O(batch).

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** lazy ranks and conditional reorder for order-preserving left batches of join-many.
**Allowed changes:** `JoinManyState::apply_left`, `apply_right` (call shape only) and `update_key` in `crates/src/collections/join/affected_key.rs`.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** right-batch skipping, `desired_order` itself, group locking.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{joins,join_many_right_moves,ordered_emission_relations,relation_operator_costs,index_contract_harness,subset_operator_indexes}`; clippy/fmt. Bench `operator_updates` (left-join-many) and `joins` vs base. Pass: left-join-many update >=10x faster; join loads not slower >10% on rerun.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

left_join_many update from 550 us to a few us.
